title: Complexity of Deciding PSD Polynomial Sum-of-Squares

problemStatement.plain: What is the computational complexity of deciding if a given PSD polynomial is a sum of squares.

knowledge.progressSummary: Session (researcher-1, 2026-06-24): proved Robinson's polynomial is NOT a sum of squares of polynomials with a fully elementary, 0-axiom Lean proof (new child entry hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-03, Proofs/Hilbert17RobinsonNotSOS.lean) and wired it into the parent, discharging the axiom robinson_not_sos_aux (parent axiomCount 4 → 3). Route: degree bound (each qᵢ deg ≤ 3) + homogeneous reduction R = Σ(comp₃ qᵢ)² + the cubic forms vanish at R's ten real projective zeros + the 10×10 evaluation matrix of cubic monomials has determinant 128 ≠ 0, so each cubic form is 0, forcing R = 0 (contra R(1,0,0)=1). This CORRECTS the earlier survey that judged Robinson non-SOS to need multi-session Gram-matrix/dual-functional machinery — the elementary zero-set route works. Remaining 3 parent axioms (univariate_psd_is_sos_aux, quadratic_psd_is_sos_aux, pfister_bound_aux) are the genuinely deep independent ones.

insights: Robinson non-SOS has an elementary zero-set proof: R's ten real projective zeros (1,±1,0),(1,0,±1),(0,1,±1),(1,±1,±1) impose ten INDEPENDENT conditions on the ten-dimensional space of ternary cubic forms (the 10×10 evaluation matrix has determinant 128 ≠ 0), so any cubic form in an SOS decomposition of R must be zero. The coefficient-cascade method (which works for Motzkin) genuinely fails for Robinson because its pure powers x⁶,y⁶,z⁶ have nonzero coefficients — but the zero-set method sidesteps that entirely.
Motzkin non-negativity is a polynomial AM–GM inequality that nlinarith closes from square hints (x²y²−1)², (x²y−y)², (xy²−x)²; no transcendental cube-root argument is needed at the eval level.

Robinson's polynomial equals Schur's expression a(a−b)(a−c)+… under a=x², b=y², c=z²≥0, so its non-negativity is exactly Schur's inequality — nlinarith finds the constrained certificate from a·(a−b)² ≥ 0 terms.

Three of the parent hilbert-17 axioms were redundant restatements, not independent assumptions: artin_hilbert17 and cassels_bound_bivariate are specializations of pfister_bound_aux (take m=2^n; and 2^2=4 defeq gives the n=2 case directly), and artin_univariate is the algebraMap image of the stronger polynomial result univariate_psd_is_sos_aux. All three now derived as theorems — axiom count 7 → 4.

Eliminating a redundant axiom is honest axiom reduction: when axiom B is provable from axiom A already in the file, B was never adding assumptive content, so converting B to `theorem ... := <derivation>` genuinely shrinks the independent-assumption set.

Assess quadratic_psd_is_sos_aux (PSD quadratic form = SOS via Gram/Cholesky / eigendecomposition over ℝ).
